questionText:
In each of the following questions, find out which part has an error.

The man who (a) / they thought to be (b) / a gentleman turned out (c) / to be a rouge (d).
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is option 1) i.e. (a).

Explanation

  • In the given sentence, change 'who' into 'whom' because we need a relative pronoun for an object.
  • When we replace 'who' by 'whom', then 'whom' refers to the man and is the object of 'thought' in the subordinate clause.
  • The relative pronoun (who/which/that) is used as a subject in the subordinate clause.
  • The relative pronoun (whom/which/that) is used as an object in the subordinate clause.
  • Hence, the relative pronoun 'whom' is correct grammatically.


The correct sentence: "The man whom they thought to be a gentleman turned out to be a rouge."


  • Who as a Subjective Pronoun:
    • 'Who' is used to provide more information about a person or people mentioned previously in a sentence. It is also a subjective pronoun. A subjective pronoun is a pronoun (I, me, he, she, etc.) that is used as the subject of the sentence. Who replaces the subject of the sentence.
    • For example, "I met Anand, who was returning from college."
  • Whom as an Objective Pronoun
    • 'Whom' is an objective pronoun that is used for formal English. It is used as the object of a verb or preposition. Whom should replace the object of the sentence. Consider who is having something done to them when finding the object of the sentence. The object is the person, place, or thing that something is being done to.
    • For example, "I have a daughter whom I love very much."

  • When in doubt, try this simple trick:
    • Use the “he/him” or “she/her” rule.
    • If it is either “he” or “she” then it should be 'who'.
    • If it is “him” or “her” then 'whom' should be used.

questionText:
Choose the word which is nearly opposite in meaning to the given word:-

Acrimonious
solutionExplanation:
Explanation

The correct answer is option 4 i.e. Harmonious.

  • Acrimonious means angry and bitter.
  • Let us take a look at what the options mean:
  1. Legal: relating to the law.
  2. Severe: bad or undesirably intense.
  3. Cursive: writing with characters joined.

Therefore 'harmonious' is opposite to the word 'acrimonious.'

questionText:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

(निष्पक्ष) Example: A good judge must remain impartial when deciding a case. "Neutral" refers to not taking sides in a dispute or war; remaining unbiased or detached. questionText:
From the options given below choose the correct idiom to fill in the blank.

Do you ___________ the long-distance telephone calls which you make in your office each month?
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is 'keep track of.'

Key Points

  • The phrase 'to keep track of' is used to mean to maintain a record.
    • For example, 'His job is to keep track of all the shipments going out to customers.'
  • In the given sentence, we can understand that the speaker is asking the other person if they keep a record of some specific calls that they make.
  • So, the correct idiom that would fill in the blanks is to keep track of.
  • Correct Sentence: Do you keep track of the long-distance telephone calls which you make in your office each month?

Hence, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

  • Let us take a look at the meanings and usage of the other idioms in the options:
    • draw a blank ⇒ elicit no successful response.
      • For example, 'The police investigated the case but drew a blank. That's why the court transferred it to the CBI.'
    • borrow a leaf out of ⇒ to do the same thing as someone did.
      • For example, 'I decided to take/borrow a leaf out of my brother's book and invest some money in the stock market.'
    • drop in ⇒ to make a casual or informal visit to a person or place.
      • For example, 'Drop in whenever you're in the neighbourhood. My house is always open for you.'

questionText:
The following question consists of an incomplete sentence or a sentence split into four parts. All four parts are jumbled up and are named P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Arrange the jumbled parts of the sentence and find out which of the four combinations from the given options will correctly complete the sentence.

A Swiss company _________________electric car batteries

P: has built what is being called a giant water battery
Q: deep under the Alps
R: that provides energy storage capacity
S: equivalent to 400,000
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is "PQRS"

Key Points

  • The sentence starts with "A Swiss company" which is a noun and a noun is followed by a verb.
  • "has" is an auxiliary verb in part P, so part P will come next.
  • Part Q will be the next part because it states where the water battery is located which was mentioned in Part P
  • Part R, Part S and the rest of the sentence provide further details about the giant water battery.
Hence, the complete sentence: A Swiss company P: has built what is being called a giant water battery Q: deep under the Alps R: that provides energy storage capacity S: equivalent to 400,000 electric car batteries
Additional Information
  • I n a grammatically correct sentence, nouns and pronouns are generally followed by a verb or an auxiliary verb.
  • Examples:
    • She goes to the market.
    • India is a country full of talent.
    • They have a huge box of fruits.

questionText:
Choose the correct option which has the same relation as that given in the words.

Extravagant : Frugal :: Reticent : _______
solutionExplanation:
Here the correct answer is Garrulous.
Key Points:-
  • The above-given pair of words i.e. Extravagant: Frugal are antonyms of each other.
  • Thus, we need an antonym for Reticent.
  • Reticent(adjective) - not revealing one's thoughts or feelings readily.
    • For Example - She was extremely reticent about her personal affairs.
  • Introverted, diffident, and taciturn are synonyms of Reticent.
  • The correct antonym of Reticent is Garrulous.
  • Garrulous(adjective) - excessively talkative, especially on trivial matters.
    • For Example - He met a garrulous cab driver.
  • Thus, the correct answer is Option 3.


Therefore, the correct pair will be Extravagant: Frugal:: Reticent: Garrulous.

  • ऊपर दिए गए शब्दों की जोड़ी यानी Extravagant: Frugal एक दूसरे के विलोम हैं।
  • इस प्रकार, हमें reticent के लिए एक एंटोनिम की आवश्यकता है।
  • Reticent(विशेषण) - किसी के विचारों या भावनाओं को आसानी से प्रकट नहीं करना।
    • उदाहरण के लिए - She was extremely reticent about her personal affairs.
  • Introverted, diffident, और taciturn 'reticent' के पर्यायवाची हैं।
  • Reticent का सही विलोम garrulous है ।
  • Garrulous(विशेषण) - अत्यधिक बातूनी, विशेष रूप से तुच्छ मामलों पर।
    • उदाहरण के लिए - He met a garrulous cab driver.
  • अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 3 है।


अत: सही युग्म होगा Extravagant: Frugal:: Reticent: Garrulous.

questionText:
Direction: The given idiom is followed by four meanings. Choose the one which best expresses the meaning of the given idiom:-

Take the bull by the horns
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is- 'To meet the danger boldly.'

Key Points

  • The meaning of the idiom 'Take the bull by the horns' is to deal decisively with a difficult or dangerous situation.
    • Idiom 'Take the bull by the horns' का अर्थ एक कठिन या खतरनाक स्थिति से निर्णायक रूप से निपटना है।
      • Example: She decided to take the bull by the horns and organize things for herself.
  • Therefore, the option which best expresses the meaning of the given idiom is "To meet the danger boldly."

Additional Information

  • The expression "Take the bull by the horns" probably originated in the American West where it was a common, but dangerous, practice to wrestle with steers.
  • This was not only done for entertainment at rodeos but was part of the everyday working life of ranchers and cowhands throughout the west.

questionText:

questionText:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Break a leg

options.text: Give advice on maintaining physical health.
Encourage someone to engage in risky activities.
Suggest taking a short break during work.
Wish someone good luck before a performance.

solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is: Option 4.

Key Points

  • The idiom "Break a leg" means to wish someone good luck before a performance. (अभिनय से पहले किसी को शुभकामनाएं देना)
    • Example: The director told the actors to break a leg before they went on stage.
  • Hence, we can infer that the correct meaning of 'Break a leg' is 'Wish someone good luck before a performance.' (अभिनय से पहले किसी को शुभकामनाएं देना)
    • Example: She told her friend to break a leg before his big audition.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Option 1: Give advice on maintaining physical health (शारीरिक स्वास्थ्य बनाए रखने के लिए सलाह देना)
    • Example: The doctor gave me advice on maintaining physical health.
  • Option 2: Encourage someone to engage in risky activities (किसी को जोखिम भरे कार्यों में शामिल होने के लिए प्रोत्साहित करना)
    • Example: He encouraged his friends to engage in risky activities like skydiving.

    • Example: The manager suggested taking a short break during work to stay fresh.

questionText:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

My partner's parents /, particularly both my father-in-laws /, bring diverse perspectives / and enriching stories to our family gatherings.

options.text: and enriching stories to our family gatherings

solutionExplanation:
The erroneous part is 'particularly my father-in-laws'.

Key Points

  • The error in the sentence lies in the incorrect plural form used for "father-in-law."
  • When referring to more than one father-in-law, the plural form should be "fathers-in-law." This is a compound noun where "father" is the main noun, and "in-law" specifies the relationship.
  • To indicate multiple individuals fitting this description, "fathers-in-law" is the appropriate plural form.
  • For instance:
    • Singular: My father-in-law is a retired professor.
    • Plural: Both my fathers-in-law are avid travelers.
  • Therefore, in the sentence provided, the correct phrase should be "particularly my fathers-in-law" to accurately refer to multiple individuals who are fathers-in-law within the context.

Correct Sentence: My partner's parents, particularly both my fathers-in-law, bring diverse perspectives and enriching stories to our family gatherings.

questionText:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The little boy / hurted himself / when he fell off / his bicycle.
solutionExplanation:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: hurted himself

Key Points

  • Replace 'hurted' with 'hurt' to make the sentence correct.
  • Hurt (verb) means to cause physical pain or injury.
  • The given sentence is written in the past tense and the past and past participle form of the verb is also 'hurt'.
  • There is no word such as 'hurted' in English grammar.

Therefore, the correct answer is option 2, which contains an error.

Corrected sentence: The little boy hurt himself when he fell off his bicycle.

questionText:
Choose the correctly spelt word:-

'God is Dead' is a ___________ statement.
solutionExplanation:
Explanation

The correct spelling is option 3 i.e. blasphemous.

  • Blasphemous refers to the action or offense of speaking sinfully about God or sacred things.
  • In this case it would mean making a statement like 'God is dead' would be offensive.
  • An example is as follows: The book was declared blasphemous and all copies ordered to be burnt.

​

  • Blasphemous is the adjective form of the word 'blasphemy.'

Therefore, the statement would read: 'God is dead is a blasphemous statement.'

questionText:
In the following items, each passage consists of six sentences. The first sentence (S1) and the final sentence (S6) are given. The middle four sentences in each have been removed and jumbled up. These are labelled P, Q, R and S. You are required to find out the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

S1: Unity in diversity is a unique feature of India
P: They should, therefore, first try to know the mind and spirit of India - the Indian-ethos, so to say.
Q: Nehru has referred to this unity very feelingly in 'The Discovery of India'.
R: Those who do not see this underlying unity in apparent diversity fail to understand this country properly.
S: Then, they will discern strands of common heritage running all through the differences of language, dress, food, method of worship etc.
S6: Have you read this book ? If not, you should do so now.
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is "RPSQ"

Key Points

  • Sentence S1 introduces the concept of unity in diversity as a unique feature of India.
  • Sentence R explains that those who fail to see the underlying unity in the apparent diversity of India fail to understand the country properly.
  • Sentence P and S advise that in order to understand India properly, one should try to know the mind and spirit of India, the "Indian-ethos," and look for strands of common heritage running through the differences in language, dress, food, and method of worship.
  • Sentence Q mentions that Jawaharlal Nehru, India's first prime minister, has referred to this unity very feelingly in his book "The Discovery of India." Sentence S6 recommends reading this book as a way to gain a better understanding of India.
  • When these sentences are put in this order, they form a coherent and logical paragraph about the importance of understanding the unity in diversity of India in order to properly understand the country.

Thus, option 4 is the correct answer.

Correct paragraph: S1 Unity in diversity is a unique feature of India R Those who do not see this underlying unity in apparent diversity fail to understand this country properly. P They should, therefore, first try to know the mind and spirit of India - the Indian-ethos, so to say. S Then, they will discern strands of common heritage running all through the differences of language, dress, food, method of worship etc. Q Nehru has referred to this unity very feelingly in 'The Discovery of India'. S6 Have you read this book ? If not, you should do so now.

questionText:
Identify the segment in the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

The Prime Minister, along with the other ministers have left for the USA to attend an important meeting.

options.text: for the USA to attend an important meeting

solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is 'the other minister have left'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
  • Here, 'the other minister has left' should be used instead of 'the other minister have left'.
  • When 'along with' is used to join two subjects then the verb that follows will be according to the first subject and in this case, it is 'The Prime Minister' which is singular.
  • So, the singular verb 'has' will be used.

Correct Sentence: The Prime Minister, along with the other ministers has left for the USA to attend an important meeting.

questionText:
Some parts of a sentence have been jumbled up, and labelled P, Q, R and S. Select the option that gives the correct sequence in which these parts can be rearranged to form a meaningful and grammatically sentence.

The retail landscape has drastically changed _______________ pressures of economic slump.

P. as it is accelerated by the global pandemic and the

Q. due to the proliferation of e-commerce,

R. replacing traditional brick and mortar stores,

S. now people are opting for online shopping for convenience
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is “QRSP”.

Key Points

  • The sentence starts with 'Q'- "due to the proliferation of e-commerce" as it introduces the main factor that has brought changes in the retail landscape.
  • R - "replacing traditional brick and mortar stores" provides the next logical connection as it says the increase in e-commerce has replaced traditional stores.
  • S - "now people are opting for online shopping for convenience" sequentially follows 'R' providing an insight into how e-commerce is changing the retail landscape.
  • Finally, P - "as it is accelerated by the global pandemic and the" suits the final place in the sequence as it provides the reasoning behind the switch to e-commerce.
  • Hence, the correct answer is 'Option 1'.

questionText:
Direction : In the following sentence choose the antonym to the underlined word:

We should strive for the country's development.
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is 'Retrogression' (Option 1)

Key Points

  • The word 'development' refers to the act of growing, advancing, or making progress.
  • The antonym of 'development' would be a word that signifies decline, or backward movement.
  • 'Retrogression' fits because it refers to the process of returning to an earlier state, typically a worse one.
  • 'Retrogression' precisely provides the opposite meaning and is an appropriate antonym.
  • The action of striving for development implies moving forward, hence its antonym would imply moving backward or regressing.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

  • 'Transgression' refers to an act that goes against a law, rule, or code of conduct.
  • 'Impurity' is the quality or condition of being impure, particularly in a physical or moral sense.
  • 'Progress' would be a synonym, not an antonym, as it refers to forward or onward movement to a destination.

questionText:
Direction: In the following question, there is a related pair of words given. Each pair is followed by four other pairs of words. Choose the pair from the given option the pair of words that best expresses the relationship like the original pair.

Desolate : Cheerful
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is “Constant : Unstable”

Key Points

  • The words 'Desolate' and 'Cheerful' are Antonyms.
    • Desolate: It means, feeling very sad and lonely for a long time.
    • Cheerful: Feeling of happiness.
  • Similarly, the words 'Constant' and 'Unstable' are antonyms.
    • Constant: A constant is an object or value that always remains the same.
    • Unstable: You can describe something as unstable if it is prone to sudden change.
  • Therefore, 'Constant' and 'Unstable' have the same relationship as 'Desolate' and 'Cheerful'

Hence, the correct pair is 'Constant: Unstable'

Additional Information

Let's discuss the other options. The words given in the other options are synonyms.

  1. Industrious and Laborious (परिश्रमी और मेहनती): If you describe someone as 'Industrious' and 'Laborious', you mean that he works very hard.
  2. Abridge and Curtail (घटाना और कम करना): If you 'abridge' and 'curtail' something, you reduce or limit it.
  3. Extinct and Lost (विलुप्त और दुर्लभ): It means, no longer in use or no longer in existence.

questionText:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word from the given options.

A light breeze _______ the forest fire and made it more dangerous.
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is 'fanned.'

Key Points

  • Let's discuss the marked option first:
    • Fanned (verb) means 'to make a fire burn more strongly by blowing on it (हवा करके आग को भड़काना)'.
      • Example: Gusty winds fanned the flames.
    • Explanation: A light wind made the forest fire more strong by blowing and hence, made it more dangerous.
  • It is clear that the words given in option 3 fit in the blanks contextually.

Therefore, the correct answer is option 3.

Complete Sentence: A light breeze fanned the forest fire and made it more dangerous.

Additional Information

  • Give up means to stop trying to do something; to accept that one cannot do something (कुछ करने की कोशिश को रोक देना; किसी काम को करने में अपनी असमर्थता को मान लेना).
  • Riled up means to make agitated and angry; upset (किसी व्‍यक्ति को उत्तेजित और क्रोधित कर देना; परेशान कर देना).
  • Enrage means to make somebody very angry (किसी व्‍यक्ति को बहुत ग़ुस्‍सा दिलाना, अत्‍यधिक क्रोधित कर देना).

questionText:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.

The church decided not to tolerate any action or offence of speaking sacrilegiously about God or sacred things.
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is: Blasphemy.

Key Points

  • The word "tolerate" means to allow or accept something, even if it is not ideal. (सहन करना)
    • Example: The teacher decided to tolerate the noise in the classroom for the day.
  • "Blasphemy" refers to the act or offense of speaking sacrilegiously about God or sacred things. (ईश्वर या पवित्र वस्तुओं के प्रति अपमानजनक बातें करना)
    • Example: The writer was accused of blasphemy for his controversial book.
  • Hence, the correct one-word substitute for the given group of words is Blasphemy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Blasphemy.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Sin (पाप): An act that is considered morally wrong or against religious law.
    • Example: According to many religions, stealing is a sin.
  • Goodness (भलाई): The quality of being morally good or virtuous.
    • Example: Her goodness was evident in the way she helped others.
  • Hatred (घृणा): Intense dislike or ill will.
    • Example: There was no hatred in her heart despite the wrongs done to her.

questionText:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word from the given options.

Alcohol deaddiction centers try to_______behavioral changes in the lifestyle of addicts by keeping them busy in various activities.
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is option 1; Use "bring about" instead of "bring in"

Key Points

  • We will have to use bring about meaning cause something to happen to make the sentence meaningful.
  • Alcohol deaddiction centres keep addicts busy in various activities and try to bring about behavioral changes in them.

Correct sentence - Alcohol deaddiction centers try to bring about behavioral changes in the lifestyle of addicts by keeping them busy in various activities.

Additional InformationPhrasal verb is a combination of words (a verb+preposition) that when used together, usually take on a different meaning than that of the original verb

  • Important phrasal verbs formed with the help of "bring"
    1. Bring about = to make something happen.
    2. Bring back = To cause someone to remember
    3. Bring forward = To make something happen earlier than originally planned.
    4. Bring off = To succeed in doing something difficult
    5. Bring on = To cause something to happen especially something bad.
    6. Bring in = To use the skills of a particular group or person.
    7. Bring out = 1. To produce a new product and start selling it. 2. To make someone or something show a quality that they have.
    8. Bring up = 1. To look after a child until He/she becomes an adult. 2. To start discussing a topic.

questionText:
Direction: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word from the given options.

There are several ways of ______________ the price at which a product can be marketed.
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is- 'determining.'

Key Points

  • Let us see the meanings of the given options:
    • Judging: to form or give an opinion about somebody/something based on the information you have. (प्राप्‍त जानकारी के आधार पर किसी व्‍यक्ति या वस्‍तु के विषय में राय बनाना या देना; आँकना)
    • Evaluating: to study the facts and then form an opinion about something. (तथ्‍यों के आधार पर मूल्‍यांकन करना)
    • Determining: to ascertain or establish exactly by research or calculation. (अनुसंधान या गणना द्वारा ठीक से पता लगाना या स्थापित करना)
